name: TC74 digital temperature sensor
description: Microchip tiny serial digital thermal sensor: reports temperature as one signed byte, 1 °C per step (-40 to 125 °C operating, ±2 °C from 25 to 85 °C, ±3 °C from 0 to 125 °C), about 8 conversions a second, over SMBus/I2C up to 100 kHz. Runs on 2.7–5.5 V at 200 µA (5 µA in standby). Needs external pull-ups on SDA and SCLK. Sold as: Microchip TC74A0-3.3VAT in a 5-pin TO-220 package (pins 1–5 with the printed face towards you, legs down: NC, SDA, GND, SCLK, VDD; tab = GND), I2C address 0x48 fixed by the A0 part number (TC74A5 = default 0x4D, A0–A7 = 0x48–0x4F).
eli5: A small thermometer chip in a power-transistor style package; your board asks it for the temperature over two wires and gets back a whole number of degrees.

pins.name: SDA
pins.description: Pin 2: SMBus/I2C data, open-drain: needs an external pull-up to VDD (4.7k)

pins.name: GND
pins.description: Pin 3: ground (the metal tab is also GND)

pins.name: SCLK
pins.description: Pin 4: SMBus/I2C clock input, 10–100 kHz: needs an external pull-up to VDD (4.7k)

pins.name: VDD
pins.description: Pin 5: supply, 2.7–5.5 V. Use the microcontroller's 3.3 V: at 5 V the inputs need 4 V for a logic high

buildNotes: Pin order (TO-220, printed face towards you, legs down, left to right): 1 NC, 2 SDA, 3 GND, 4 SCLK, 5 VDD. The metal tab is tied to GND: do not let it touch other wires.

The legs are on a 1.7 mm pitch, not 2.54 mm: bend them alternately forward and back (staggered, as the circuit-board footprint expects) to fit a breadboard or PCB, and check that no two legs share a row.
SDA and SCLK need pull-up resistors to VDD (4.7k each); the chip has none inside.
Power VDD from 3.3 V on a 3.3 V microcontroller: its logic-high threshold is 0.8 × VDD (4 V at a 5 V supply), so 3.3 V signals are not reliable with a 5 V supply.
The bus must run at 100 kHz or slower (minimum 10 kHz): create the I2C bus with freq=100000.
The address is fixed by the part number: TC74A0 = 0x48, TC74A1 = 0x49 ... TC74A5 = 0x4D (the most common default) ... TC74A7 = 0x4F. Run i2c.scan() if unsure.
Temperature: read one byte from command 0x00; it is two's complement in whole °C (0x19 = 25 °C, 0xE7 = -25 °C). The chip rounds down: 25.75 °C reads 25, -0.25 °C reads -1.
Wait up to 250 ms after power-up for the first conversion (CONFIG bit 6 DATA_RDY = 1). Writing 0x80 to CONFIG (0x01) enters 5 µA standby; write 0x00 to resume.

driver.code:
# TC74 tiny serial digital thermal sensor (Microchip DS21462D), MicroPython driver.
# SMBus/I2C, 10-100 kHz only. Command byte (register): 0x00 RTR = TEMP (read-only),
# 0x01 RWCR = CONFIG (D7 SHDN: 1 = standby, D6 DATA_RDY: 1 = ready, read-only).
# TEMP: one byte, two's complement, 1 degC per LSB (0x19 = 25 C, 0xE7 = -25 C).
# The chip rounds down: 25.75 C reads 25, -0.25 C reads -1 (Table 4-4).
# Address 1001 A2A1A0 is set by the part number: TC74A0 = 0x48 ... TC74A5 = 0x4D (default) ... TC74A7 = 0x4F.
import time

_RTR = 0x00
_RWCR = 0x01
_SHDN = 0x80
_DATA_RDY = 0x40


class TC74:
    def __init__(self, i2c, addr=0x48):
        self.i2c = i2c
        self.addr = addr

    def config(self, value=None):
        """Read (no argument) or write the CONFIG register."""
        if value is None:
            return self.i2c.readfrom_mem(self.addr, _RWCR, 1)[0]
        self.i2c.writeto_mem(self.addr, _RWCR, bytes([value & _SHDN]))

    def ready(self):
        """True once a conversion has finished since power-up or leaving standby."""
        return bool(self.config() & _DATA_RDY)

    def wait_ready(self, timeout_ms=300):
        """Wait for DATA_RDY (datasheet: at most 250 ms after power-on). Returns True if ready."""
        t0 = time.ticks_ms()
        while not self.ready():
            if time.ticks_diff(time.ticks_ms(), t0) > timeout_ms:
                return False
            time.sleep_ms(10)
        return True

    def temperature(self):
        """Temperature in whole degC (Read Byte, command 0x00, two's complement)."""
        raw = self.i2c.readfrom_mem(self.addr, _RTR, 1)[0]
        return raw - 256 if raw & 0x80 else raw

    def standby(self, on=True):
        """SHDN = 1: A/D halted, TEMP frozen, about 5 uA. SHDN = 0: normal, 8 samples/s."""
        self.config(_SHDN if on else 0)

example.code:
from machine import I2C, Pin
import time
from tc74 import TC74

i2c = I2C({I2C_ID}, sda=Pin({SDA}), scl=Pin({SCL}), freq=100000)  # TC74: 100 kHz max
sensor = TC74(i2c, 0x48)  # TC74A0; a TC74A5 is 0x4D
sensor.wait_ready()  # first conversion: up to 250 ms after power-up
while True:
    print('T=%dC' % sensor.temperature())
    time.sleep(1)
